author: context-engineering-agent
phase: Phase 7 - Agent-Task Routing (AR.3 per-story context window design, Sprint 2)
depends_on: docs/phase-7-routing/ar3_context_windows.json v1.0.0 (classification model and per-story context-window method reused verbatim from Sprint 1; not re-derived)
methodology_reuse_note: Same per-story context-window design method as ar3_context_windows.json: sources are the exact HLD section / SRS-AC / backlog-AC / AR1 must-not-deviate citations the story's own routing record names, never invented additions. context_budget_tokens is a judgment call scaled to how much real source content (HLD prose + pseudocode/tables, ACs, must_not_deviate items, cross-references) the story actually cites, following the same 3500-7000 band Sprint 1 used, not a fixed formula.

classification_model.name: Bell-LaPadula classification-ceiling (carried forward from ar3_context_windows.json, now with Zone 5 activated)
classification_model.rule: No story's context window may include Zone 2 (Episodic) or Zone 5 (Entity) content bearing PII unless the story itself is security-cleared. No Sprint 2 story is security-cleared for raw PII read access. Where a story's implementation reasoning needs to reference Zone 2/5 content shape, a redacted/pseudonymized synthetic example is substituted for any real or realistic PII value - this explicitly includes an HLD-authored illustrative example that uses realistic-looking names/places (e.g. the Section 3.4 'Sachin lives in Mumbai' worked example), not only literal user data.
classification_model.zone_5_activation_note: ar3_context_windows.json recorded Zone 5 as 'N/A-not-yet-applicable' because FR-005 was out of Sprint 1 scope. Sprint 2 ships Zone 5 (DASH-STORY-017), so the Zone 5 half of the ceiling is now LIVE, not hypothetical: DASH-STORY-017 is the first story in either sprint where the Bell-LaPadula ceiling actually fires on Zone 5 content, and is treated with the same strictest-redaction discipline ar3_context_windows.json applied to Zone 2 (DASH-STORY-003) and Zone 6-over-Zone-2 (DASH-STORY-007).
classification_model.zone_3_extension_note: Zone 3 (Semantic) is not itself named in the ceiling rule, but HLD Section 3.4's owned entities (SemanticEdge subject_ref/predicate/object_ref, GeneralFact statement) are directly about entities and the HLD's own worked example pairs a realistic person-name with a location. Per Hard Rule 2 (HLD Section 3.10) Zone 3 never copies an entity attribute value - only entity_id references - so it does not hold Zone 5's raw attribute PII, but its relationship-fact content is treated with the same redaction caution as a Zone 2/5-adjacent zone for any story whose decisive content is the worked example itself (DASH-STORY-012, DASH-STORY-013).
classification_model.zone_8_extension_note: Zone 8 (Consolidation) is not named in the ceiling rule either, but ADR-009's own India Layer text calls it out explicitly: 'Zone 8 holds the longest-lived PII' and requires per-subject destroyable encryption keys for crypto-shredding erasure. DASH-STORY-018 (the store) and DASH-STORY-020 (the erasure cascade) are treated with ceiling-equivalent discipline even though the rule's literal text names only Zones 2 and 5.

context_windows.title: Zone 3 Semantic Memory store - SemanticEdge and GeneralFact schema with non-duplication CHECK constraint
context_windows.pii_note: Zone 3's owned entities (SemanticEdge subject_ref/predicate/object_ref, GeneralFact statement) are relationship facts about real-world entities, and HLD Section 3.4's own worked example is a realistic name-plus-location pair ('Sachin lives in Mumbai' -> SemanticEdge(located_in, Sachin, Mumbai)). Per the classification model's synthetic-example rule this is substituted with a pseudonymized entity placeholder (e.g. <ENTITY_A>/<ENTITY_B>) wherever the schema-design rationale is illustrated in this context window - the literal HLD names are not carried into the implementer's context. Per Hard Rule 2 (HLD 3.10), Zone 3 never copies an attribute value from Zone 5, so the schema itself stores entity_id references, not raw PII attribute content; the CHECK constraint and non-duplication design are schema-shape decisions that do not require any real fact content to specify.

context_windows.title: EntityOwnershipSpecification classification gate (|subjects|==0, |subjects|>1, conditional |subjects|==1 index_reverse sub-branch)
context_windows.pii_note: This story's decisive content IS the Sachin/Mumbai worked example - the |subjects|==1,|objects|==1 branch and its index_reverse=true/false sub-cases are defined entirely in terms of it. The routing table (the |subjects|==0/>1/==1 branching logic itself) is structural pseudocode, not PII, and is admitted verbatim. The illustrative worked example is admitted with the entity names replaced by pseudonymized placeholders (<ENTITY_A> for 'Sachin', <PLACE_A> for 'Mumbai'), consistent with the classification model's rule that a realistic-looking synthetic example is treated the same as real PII for redaction purposes. The context window explicitly excludes any Zone 5 attribute-write implementation detail, since that branch is out of this story's build scope (must_not_deviate).

context_windows.title: Zone 3 to Zone 6 retrieval-index projection (async event emission only)
context_windows.pii_note: The projected items originate in Zone 3, which per the DASH-STORY-012/013 entries above can carry entity-relationship content. This story's own scope is strictly the async event-publish mechanics (EventBus wiring, non-blocking durability independence per OAQ-16) - it does not read, transform, or log the Zone 3 item's fact content, only its event envelope (item_id, zone, per HLD Section 7.6's memory.written contract shape). No fact content or entity name is admitted into this context window; nothing needed redaction beyond confirming the exclusion, the same posture ar3_context_windows.json used for DASH-STORY-009's rotation-sweep wiring.

context_windows.title: Procedural Memory zone (Zone 4) core store, point lookup, and Importance ratio
context_windows.pii_note: Zone 4 owns Procedure records (task_signature_hash, steps[], success_count, failure_count) - learned task/tool-use procedures, not conversational or entity-attribute content. HLD Section 3.10's Data Ownership Map records no READS line for Zone 4 and Section 10's asset list does not name it among the flagged PII-bearing stores the way it does Zones 2, 5 and 8. The classification model's ceiling is scoped to Zone 2/Zone 5 (and, by extension in this file, Zone 8); Zone 4's own content does not trigger it, so no redaction was necessary for this story's schema, point-lookup, or Importance-ratio content.

context_windows.title: Zone 4 (Procedural) capacity cap and MaxAge rotation backstop wiring
context_windows.pii_note: This story evicts Zone 4 (Procedural) items only, ranked by MemoryScore - unlike its Sprint 1 analogue DASH-STORY-004, which evicted Zone 2 (PII-bearing Episodic) items and therefore carried a REDACTED DPDP acceptance criterion (AC-002-CAP-DPDP-1). DASH-STORY-016 has no DPDP acceptance criterion attached (confirmed in sprint2_ar1_assignments.json's p1_trigger_evaluation for this story) because Zone 4 content is not classification-ceiling material. No redaction was required.

context_windows.title: Entity Memory zone (Zone 5) - canonical per-entity attribute store with sub-record provenance and alias Trie resolution
context_windows.pii_note: Zone 5 is the classification model's other explicitly-named ceiling zone, and this is the story that activates it for real in either sprint (Sprint 1 recorded it as N/A-not-yet-applicable). EntityRecord's attributes{attr -> {value, provenance_id, updated_at}} shape is, by HLD Section 3.6's own description, the canonical sole-owner store for a real entity's real attribute values - exactly the content class the ceiling exists to protect. This context window admits only the structural shape: the point-lookup index design, the per-attribute sub-record provenance write pattern (one new provenance record per attribute, no whole-record rewrite), and the Trie prefix-match mechanism for alias resolution - no real or realistic attribute value (name, address, phone, or any other entity attribute) is included anywhere, and no worked example is illustrated with a concrete value the way DASH-STORY-012/013 illustrate Zone 3's routing logic. This is the strictest redaction discipline in this Sprint 2 file, matching the treatment ar3_context_windows.json gave DASH-STORY-003 and DASH-STORY-007 for their direct/indirect Zone 2 exposure.

context_windows.title: Zone 8 Consolidation store - object-store blobs with hot manifest index (ADR-009)
context_windows.pii_note: Zone 8 receives archived items from Zones 2/3/4/5 and ADR-009's India Layer states outright that 'Zone 8 holds the longest-lived PII.' This context window admits only the manifest/index shape (item_id -> (blob_id, byte_range, compression_generation) resolution, per AC-008-1) and the tenant-uniformity merge-assertion and degraded-mode control logic (AC-008-2..4) - never decoded blob content, which is opaque compressed payload the implementer's own adapter code does not need to inspect to satisfy these ACs. This story is P1-gated (api-security-auditor, Maker-Checker per sprint2_ar1_assignments.json) on the cross-tenant merge risk (HLD threat I-5); the implementing agent (python-backend-engineer) is not security-cleared for raw PII, and the reviewer's separate review scope is not folded into this implementer context window.

context_windows.title: Compressed to Archived rotation transition completion
context_windows.pii_note: This story transitions items (including PII-bearing Zone 2/3/5 items already archived via DASH-STORY-018's write path) between rotation states, keyed on item_id, MemoryScore and the stored rotation deadline only - it never reads item payload content, matching ar3_context_windows.json's exact treatment of the analogous DASH-STORY-009 rotation state machine in Sprint 1. AC-008-ROT-4's post-mutation deadline requirement is a scheduling-correctness concern (ADR-012), not a content concern, so no payload example or redaction was needed beyond confirming the exclusion.

context_windows.title: DPDP erasure-cascade reach into Zone 8 archives plus India residency and crypto-shredding
context_windows.pii_note: The single most direct PII/DPDP story in Sprint 2: its own subject matter is per-subject encryption key generation/storage/destruction and India-region bucket provisioning for erasure. The context window carries the DPDP legal/technical framing (Section 10 DPDP-2/3/4, the still-open OAQ-10 legal-sufficiency question, ADR-009's India Layer text) and the key-lifecycle CONTRACT (destruction-is-erasure, no in-place blob rewrite, subject_id secondary index dependency) but never any actual or example subject_id, key material value, or archived content - the story is specified entirely in terms of mechanism and contract, not example data, so no synthetic-example substitution was even needed the way DASH-STORY-012/013/017 required one. The implementing agent (python-backend-engineer, the most marginal above-threshold score in Sprint 2 per AR1-S2-G1) is not security-cleared; the two accepted advisory reviews (crypto-security-specialist, cloud-security-architect) run in their own separate review contexts, not folded into this implementer's context window, and OAQ-10's legal question is carried as explicitly open, never asserted as resolved.

summary.zone_5_ceiling_activation: DASH-STORY-017 is the first story in either Sprint 1 or Sprint 2 where the classification model's Zone 5 ceiling is live rather than N/A-not-yet-applicable (ar3_context_windows.json's own note for Sprint 1).
summary.strictest_redaction: DASH-STORY-017 (direct Zone 5 EntityRecord activation - canonical per-entity attribute store) and DASH-STORY-020 (per-subject crypto-shredding key lifecycle and India residency, the sprint's most direct DPDP/PII subject matter) carry the strictest redaction discipline. DASH-STORY-012 and DASH-STORY-013 also required active redaction of HLD's own realistic-looking worked example (Sachin/Mumbai), substituting pseudonymized entity placeholders.
summary.note_on_security_clearance: No Sprint 2 story is security-cleared for raw PII, matching Sprint 1's posture. DASH-STORY-018's P1 reviewer (api-security-auditor) and DASH-STORY-020's two accepted advisory reviewers (crypto-security-specialist, cloud-security-architect) each operate in their own separate review context per sprint2_ar1_assignments.json - none of that reviewer-level access is granted to, or folded into, the implementing agent's (python-backend-engineer / database-engineer) context window documented here.
